The peers of your [NetBird](https://netbird.io) network in Gladys, through
the REST API of its management server (NetBird Cloud or your own server):

- each peer becomes a Gladys device: **connected**, **last seen**, **NetBird
  IP**, **client version**, **login expired** and **login expires** (the date
  its login session ends);
- the network becomes a device with its **peers connected** and its
  **peers** in total;
- three scene triggers: **Peer connected**, **Peer disconnected** and
  **Peer login expired**;
- a dashboard widget, **NetBird peers**: the connected peers with their
  NetBird IP, the disconnected ones with their last connection.

Read only: Gladys never changes anything in NetBird (no peer deleted, no
rule or group changed).

> **This integration has never been tested with a real NetBird account.**
> This first version was written from the public NetBird API reference
> (docs.netbird.io/api) and tested against a fake NetBird only. Please report
> what works and what does not on the Gladys forum.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with NetBird.

## Before you start: a token that only reads

1. In the NetBird dashboard, open **Team → Service Users** and create a
   service user `gladys` with the **Auditor** role: it reads every peer and
   changes nothing (a service user is not a person: its token does not stop
   working when someone leaves). If the Auditor role is not offered, use the
   **User** role: a service user reads every peer and the account settings
   whatever its role, and with User it can change nothing. Never Admin:
   Gladys only reads, the token needs no right to change anything.
2. Open the user, **Create Token**, name it `gladys`, pick an expiration
   and copy the token (it starts with `nbp_`): NetBird shows it only once.
3. **Not a personal token of a regular user with the User role**: such a
   token lists only the peers that user registered, and none at all when
   the account restricts the dashboard of regular users ("Restrict
   dashboard for regular users"). When the integration can tell, the
   connection status says so. A service user does not have this limit.
4. The expiration dates of the peers (login expires) come from the account
   settings: a token that may not read them leaves these dates empty, the
   rest works.

## Configuration

- **Management server**: empty for NetBird Cloud (its API is
  `https://api.netbird.io`; the dashboard address `app.netbird.io` is read as
  it).
  Self-hosted: the https address of your server, the one of the dashboard
  (`https://netbird.example.org`, a port and a path are kept, a trailing
  `/api` is dropped). `http://` is refused: the token would cross the network
  in clear.
- **Personal access token**: kept by Gladys in its database, never shown
  again, sent only to the NetBird management server, in the
  `Authorization: Token …` header (never in an address, never in a log,
  never in the `/data` volume). Paste the token alone: a space or an
  invisible character copied with it is refused with a clear message.
- **Certificate fingerprint** (optional, self-hosted only): by default the
  certificate of the server must come from a known authority (NetBird Cloud,
  Let's Encrypt). A server with its own certificate: type its SHA-256
  fingerprint; that certificate, and no other, is then accepted, checked
  before the token is sent. After a renewal, type the new one. To read it:
  your browser (padlock, certificate, SHA-256 fingerprint) or
  `openssl s_client -connect netbird.example.org:443 </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256`.
- **Groups** (optional): names or ids of NetBird groups, separated by
  commas. Only their peers become devices and are counted. Empty: every peer
  the token sees.
- **Refresh**: every minute (default) to every 10 minutes. One request per
  reading (the peers), plus the account settings once an hour, and the user
  of the token (`/api/users/current`) at start and at every new attempt after
  a failure. A service user gets 403 there: that is expected and ignored.

Then open the **Discovery** tab and create the peers and the network you
want to follow. Only the created devices get their states.

## What each feature shows

- **Connected** (1 / 0): what NetBird says about the peer right now.
  Nothing is published while NetBird does not say.
- **Last seen**: the last time the peer connected to the management server
  (or changed its status there), as `2026-10-17 08:00 UTC` (UTC, the time
  zone of NetBird). It may not move while the peer stays connected.
- **NetBird IP**: the address of the peer inside the NetBird network
  (`100.x.y.z`). Its public address is never read into Gladys.
- **Client version**: the version of the NetBird client on the peer. The API
  does not say whether an update exists: there is no "update available"
  feature in this version.
- **Login expired** (1 / 0): the login session of the peer expired; someone
  must log in again on it (`netbird up`). Only peers added through an SSO
  login expire; peers added with a setup key never do.
- **Login expires**: the date the session ends (last login plus the
  expiration of the account), `—` when it never expires, nothing while it
  cannot be known (a token that may not read the account settings).
- **Peers connected / Peers** (network device): the counts of the peers
  of the group filter (all, without a filter), including those beyond the
  500 that become devices.
- Gladys accepts 300 states per minute from an integration: this one sends
  at most 250, the counts first, then connected, then login expired, then
  the texts (in turn). With many peers created at once, the first values
  arrive over a few minutes.

## Scene triggers

- **Peer connected**: a peer that was disconnected is connected again.
- **Peer disconnected**: a connected peer is disconnected.
- **Peer login expired**: the login session of a peer just expired.

Each one carries the peer (filter: one peer, or any), its name and its
NetBird IP. They fire at the next reading after the change (up to the
refresh interval later), once per change. Never at the first reading after
a start of the integration, nor at the first reading after an outage (when
NetBird could not be read, the changes in between are unknown). A new peer
fires nothing. At most 30 events per reading.

## Dashboard widget "NetBird peers"

On the dashboard, edit, add a box, pick **NetBird peers** (it needs Gladys
5.1.0 or later). It shows, from the last reading of the integration (it
sends no request of its own):

- **tiles**: peers connected, disconnected, in total, and, when there are
  some, peers whose state NetBird does not give (**Unknown**, never red) and
  peers whose login expired;
- **a list** (8 rows at most), one row per peer: its name, a badge
  _online_ / _offline_ / _login expired_ / _unknown_, and its NetBird IP and
  DNS name, or, for a disconnected peer, the date of its last connection
  (shown by the dashboard in your time zone). Tap a row for the details: IP
  and DNS name, last connection, system, NetBird version, groups, login
  expiry. The connected peers come first, by name, then the disconnected
  ones, the most recently seen first, then the unknown ones;
- **a status**: whether NetBird answers, the time of the last reading (in
  UTC), the watched peers that are offline or not found;
- **"+N more"** when the list does not hold every peer.

Settings of the box:

- **Peers listed**: all (default), connected, or disconnected (a peer
  without a state is listed only under "all"). The counts always cover
  every peer of the groups of the box.
- **Groups** (optional): names or ids of NetBird groups, separated by
  commas, within the peers the integration follows. 100 characters at most
  (a limit of Gladys for widget settings).
- **Peers to watch** (optional): peers that should stay connected (a
  server, a NAS). When one is disconnected, the "Disconnected" tile and its
  badge turn red and the status names it ("Watched, offline"). A watched
  peer missing from the reading (deleted in NetBird, registered again under
  a new id, out of the group filter of the integration) is named in red
  too ("Watched, not found"). Only peers created as devices can be picked.
  **If you delete the Gladys device of a watched peer, the box shows an
  error** (Gladys refuses a setting that names a device that no longer
  exists): edit the box and save it again without that peer.
- **Rows shown**: 3, 5 or 8.
- **Page**: 1 by default. More than 8 peers? Add a second box on page 2.

Example (text capture, English dashboard, times in Paris):

```
[ Connected 2 ]  [ Disconnected 1 ]  [ Total 3 ]
NAS      100.92.10.1 · nas.netbird.cloud        (online)
Phone    100.92.10.3 · phone.netbird.cloud      (online)
Laptop   10/16/2026 11:30 PM                    (offline)
  ● NetBird: answers
  ● Last reading: 2026-10-17 08:00 UTC
```

With **Peers to watch** = NAS, while it is disconnected:

```
[ Connected 1 ]  [ Disconnected 2 (red) ]  [ Total 3 ]
...
  ● Watched, offline: NAS (red)
```

NetBird answers but no peer is in the view (groups of the box or of the
integration):

```
[ Connected 0 ]  [ Disconnected 0 ]  [ Total 0 ]
NetBird answers, but no peer is in this view (groups of the widget or of the integration).
  ● NetBird: answers
  ● Last reading: 2026-10-17 08:00 UTC
```

While NetBird does not answer (or a pause, or the first reading after a
restart), the same empty view says "No peer in this view (last reading)."

Once something was read, the widget keeps showing the last reading (NetBird
IPs rarely change), and its colors say how fresh it is: tiles and status in
red when NetBird does not answer ("no answer"), in orange during a pause
asked by NetBird (HTTP 429 or a 5xx server error), in blue while the first
reading after a restart is pending; the badges of the rows turn grey then
(they are what was last read). With a refused token or a configuration to
fix, or before anything was ever read with this server, groups and token, it
shows a short text instead of the peers: a new token (another account) never
shows the peers of the previous one. It is pulled again at the refresh
interval, and at once when a peer connects, disconnects, expires, logs in
again, is added, renamed or removed, or when NetBird fails or answers again
(one nudge per 10 seconds at most). It never shows
the token, the address of the server, the public IP or the location of a
peer.

## Connection problems

- **Token refused** (HTTP 401, or a 403 answered by the NetBird API itself,
  on the list of the peers: wrong, expired, revoked, or without the right to
  list peers): Gladys stops and does not try again by itself, even after a
  restart or when Gladys reconnects. Create a new token (a service user
  with the Auditor role), paste it and save the configuration: only saving
  tries again. A 403 page that does not come from the API (a proxy or a
  firewall in front of it) is retried normally. A refusal on the user of the
  token (`/api/users/current`, always 403 for a service user) never stops
  anything.
- **NetBird busy** (HTTP 429) or **server error** (HTTP 5xx): every request
  pauses, as long as NetBird asks (Retry-After) within 1 minute and 6 hours,
  never less than the refresh interval. The pause is kept in `/data`: a
  restart, a reconnection of Gladys or a saved configuration waits too.
- **NetBird unreachable** (network, timeout, certificate): retried after the
  refresh interval (one minute at least), then the delay doubles up to 30
  minutes; the devices show as unreachable meanwhile. The integration never
  gives up.
- **Certificate refused or changed**: nothing is sent. Install a certificate
  from a known authority, or type (again) the fingerprint of the server.
- **Test the connection** reads the peers again and says how many are
  connected; it never retries a refused token nor shortens a pause.

## Limits

- One NetBird account per integration; 500 peers at most become devices
  (narrow the group filter beyond; the counts include them all, but not
  those of the widget, which sees only the 500 followed).
- A peer deleted in NetBird and registered again gets a new NetBird id: it
  becomes a new device (the old one stays without values).
- The network device is one per integration (`network:main`): pointing the
  integration at another account keeps the same device.
- Read only in this version: no command (delete a peer, change a rule).
- Not tested with NetBird Cloud nor a self-hosted server, nor with the
  different roles of NetBird: see TODO.md in the repository.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que NetBird te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How it works | `section` | No | Gladys reads your NetBird network through the REST API of its management server (NetBird Cloud or your own server), with a personal access token. Each peer becomes a Gladys device (Discovery tab): connected, last seen, NetBird IP, client version, login expired and login expiry; the network becomes a device with its peers connected and in total. Read only: Gladys never changes anything in NetBird. Use the token of a service user with the Auditor role (it reads every peer and changes nothing; the User role otherwise, never Admin): the personal token of a regular user with the User role lists only that user's peers, often none (see the documentation). Unofficial integration, not affiliated with NetBird. |
| Management server (empty: NetBird Cloud) | `string` | No | Leave empty for NetBird Cloud (its API is https:\/\/api.netbird.io; the dashboard address app.netbird.io is read as it). Self-hosted: the https address of your server, the one of the dashboard (e.g. https:\/\/netbird.example.org), without /api. http:\/\/ is refused: the token would cross the network in clear. |
| Personal access token | `secret` | Sí | In the NetBird dashboard: Team, Service Users (or Users), the user, Create Token. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to the NetBird management server, in the Authorization header. |
| Certificate | `section` | No | By default the certificate of the management server must come from a known authority (NetBird Cloud, Let's Encrypt). A self-hosted server with its own certificate: type its SHA-256 fingerprint below. That certificate, and no other, is then accepted, checked before the token is sent. Leave empty for NetBird Cloud. |
| Certificate fingerprint (SHA-256, optional) | `string` | No | Pins this certificate: the server must present exactly it, even after a renewal (type the new one then). Shown by your browser (certificate details) or by openssl (see the documentation). |
| Groups (optional) | `string` | No | Names or ids of the NetBird groups to follow, separated by commas: only their peers become devices and are counted. Empty: every peer the token sees. |
| Refresh | `select` | Sí | How often Gladys reads the peers (one request each time). The scene triggers start up to this long after the change. |

## Cómo instalar NetBird en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: NetBird aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-netbird:0.1.3`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-netbird](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-netbird).

NetBird requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

NetBird es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
